Name: selective_delex_json
Title: Selective DeLex-JSON: Schema-Level Defense Against Constrained-Decoding Jailbreak Attacks
Short Hypothesis: Selectively replacing suspicious forced literals in JSON schemas with opaque placeholders (while preserving schema structure) will defend against EnumAttack-style constrained decoding jailbreaks with near-zero attack success rate and minimal benign schema false positive rate.
Related Work: CDA (ArXiv 2503.24191, 8 citations) identifies the control-plane attack surface in JSON Schema constrained decoding. EnumAttack embeds harmful prompts as forced enum values, bypassing safety alignment at 22% ASR. DictAttack achieves 75.8% ASR. StruQ (2024) uses reserved tokens plus structured instruction tuning for prompt injection defense. SecAlign (2024) uses preference optimization for robustness. Spotlighting (2024) proposes delimiting/encoding transformations. No prior work proposes schema-level preprocessing defense specifically targeting constrained decoding attacks.

notes: Defense is pure Python regex preprocessing -- zero GPU needed
Test attack/defense on Gemini's structured output API directly
Existing results: 0% ASR on HarmBench (from 22%), 1.1% FPR
Extend to test Gemini, GPT-4o, Claude for cross-model generalization
